title: Ops Card assembler with contextual signal prioritization
creator: Sana Patel
description: Build a server-side composer that aggregates prioritized signals (top spans, KV-cache deltas, anomalous metrics, and log excerpts) into a single Ops Card attachment for PagerDuty and Slack alerts. The Ops Card should be compact, actionable, and include: a short synthesis sentence, 3 prioritized evidence snippets (trace span + link, metric slice with sparkline, log excerpt), suggested runbook steps ranked by confidence, and a seeded postmortem draft link. This ticket covers schema design, runtime enrichment hooks, PD/Slack attachment format, throttling rules, and rollout steps for Canary -> Global. Goal: reduce on-call mean-time-to-detect/diagnose by surfacing the most relevant signals and remove manual evidence collection during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Schema: Ops Card JSON schema documented in Confluence with fields for summary, evidence[], runbook_recs[], postmortem_seed_url.
Runtime: trace and metric enrichment hooks implemented in runtime-proxy that can fetch top-3 spans and metric slices without blocking token generation beyond 80ms p95.
Integrations: PagerDuty attachment and Slack Block Kit view render correctly for both ephemeral and persistent alerts (verified in staging PD org and test Slack workspace).
Policy: Rate limiting & sampling rules enforced (max 1 Ops Card per 10s per service, sample bias toward error/severity-labeled incidents).
Automation: A seeded postmortem (Markdown) is auto-created and linked when a ticket is acknowledged and severity & duration thresholds are met (configurable).
Observability: Dashboard shows Ops Card generation rate, enrichment latency p50/p95/p99, and % incidents with autogenerated postmortems.
Docs & Runbooks: Confluence runbook describing how to opt-out, customize evidence extractors, and rollback plan.
